description.value: The study examined whether neural responses to high-calorie food pictures before and after a 12-week psychosocial weight-loss program predicted weight loss during treatment and weight maintenance over the following 9 months.

design.value: Longitudinal fMRI design with obese and overweight participants scanned before and after a 12-week behavioral, psychosocial weight-loss program and again assessed at a 9-month follow-up; normal-weight control participants were scanned twice 12 weeks apart without participating in the program.

description.value: Twenty-five obese (n = 21) and overweight (n = 4) adults enrolled in the 12-wk EatRight Lifestyle Weight Management Program; for brevity, this group was referred to as obese.

exclusion_criteria.value: intelligence quotient < 80 on the Shipley Institute of Living Scale
a chronic health or neurological condition
history of head injury or loss of consciousness for more than 5 min
current or past alcohol or drug abuse problem
worse than 20/40 vision not correctable with contact lenses or the non-ferromagnetic corrective glasses used at the magnet
blood pressure > 140/90 not controlled by medication
meeting the full criteria for any eating disorder
concurrently enrolled in another weight-loss program
food preferences or allergies inconsistent with the food pictures
immigrants for whom typical American foods were novel
body weight of > 350 lb (159 kg) and/or girth > 64 in (163 cm)

recruitment_method.value: Recruited at one of the first three of twelve EatRight classes.

medical_condition.value: obesity; four participants were overweight by BMI classification
two participants were taking metformin, glipizide, and/or lantus to manage Type II diabetes
three participants were being treated with antidepressants for depression

clinical_characteristics.value: Initial BMI range was 28.4 to 44.6 kg/m2, with mean ± SD 32.86 ± 3.82.

medication_status.value: Two participants were on medication for Type II diabetes. Three participants were treated with a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor and had been on medication for more than 6 months without changing medication between the first and second scanning sessions.

description.value: Thirteen normal-weight adults who did not participate in the EatRight program.

recruitment_method.value: Recruited from UAB and the surrounding community using flyers and advertisements posted in the UAB Reporter newspaper.

name.value: control participants who returned for the second scanning session

description.value: Two control participants, both men, did not return for the second scanning session; the remaining 11 controls contributed to the two-session analyses and 9-month comparison.

name.value: obese participants with 9-mo follow-up weight measurement

description.value: All but one obese participant returned for a brief lab visit 9 mo later for a final body weight measurement; the 9-mo regression analysis excluded two weight-change outliers and therefore used 22 participants, with robust regression additionally performed on all 24.

excluded_count.value: 1 did not return for follow-up; 2 weight-change outliers were excluded from the primary regression analysis

task_name.value: Viewing high-calorie food, low-calorie food, and car pictures

task_description.value: Participants viewed visual stimuli in six 3:15-min runs. Each run contained two pseudorandomly presented epochs each of car and low-calorie food images and one epoch each of high-calorie sweet and high-calorie savory food images. Each epoch lasted 21 s and contained seven images presented for 2.5 s followed by a 0.5-s gap, with 9 s of blank screen and a fixation cross between epochs.

instructions.value: Participants were instructed to eat a normal breakfast and then refrain from eating for 8 h before being imaged; they were also instructed to abstain from alcohol for 24 h, avoid exercise on the day of the study, and avoid caffeine for 3 h prior to imaging.

stimuli.value: 504 high-quality color photographs: 168 food images and 84 control images for each pre- and post-treatment session. Food images comprised 84 high-calorie images, equally divided between sweet and savory foods, and 84 low-calorie food images. Control images depicted cars.

task_performance_measures.value: Post-scan memory performance for identifying pictures seen during the fMRI scan.

task_description.value: After scanning, participants sorted 60 laminated color pictures of foods and cars into two piles: those seen in the magnet and those not seen.

instructions.value: Sort pictures into those seen in the magnet and those not seen.

stimuli.value: Sixty laminated color pictures of foods and cars; half had been presented in the magnet and half were novel.

task_performance_measures.value: Percentage of pictures correctly identified as having been seen during each fMRI scan.

instrument.value: Philips Achieva 3 T ultra-short (1.57 m) bore magnet; 6-channel or 8-channel head coil

description.value: Functional MR images were acquired using single-shot gradient echo T2*-weighted echo-planar imaging with BOLD contrast. Six runs were acquired in each session. Each run consisted of 65 volumes. The scan resolution was 80 × 79, reconstructed to 128 × 128, with a 230 × 149 × 230 mm field of view. Each volume comprised 30 axial slices, 4 mm thick with a 1 mm interslice gap. The first two scans were discarded to allow the BOLD signal to stabilize.

pulse_sequence_type.value: single-shot gradient echo T2*-weighted echo-planar imaging (EPI) with BOLD contrast

instrument.value: Philips Achieva 3 T ultra-short (1.57 m) bore magnet

description.value: High-resolution T1-weighted scans were acquired and used to exclude participants with gross brain abnormality.

Functional images were slice time-corrected, spatially realigned, normalized to standard MNI brain space, spatially smoothed, high-pass filtered, and temporally filtered using an autoregressive model.

steps.value: Slice time correction to the onset of the 15th slice (middle slice).
Spatial realignment using INRIAlign, an algorithm unbiased by local signal changes.
A mean functional image was computed for each run and matched to the EPI template provided within SPM8.
Spatial normalization to standard Montreal Neurological Institute (MNI) brain space.
Three-dimensional Gaussian spatial smoothing with a 6 mm full-width at half-maximum kernel.
High-pass filtering at 1/128 Hz to remove low-frequency artifacts.
Temporal filtering using an autoregressive AR(1) model.

model_settings.value: Separate regressors were created for high-calorie food, low-calorie food, and car images by convolving the time course of activation, using a boxcar function, with the canonical HRF. Fixed-effects analyses were performed for each participant for both imaging sessions. The high-calorie foods vs. cars and high-calorie foods vs. low-calorie foods contrasts were examined.

Second-level group analyses were performed using a random-effects model of the beta images from the single-subject contrast maps. Union masks of the single-subject contrast maps were generated for the pre-treatment and post-treatment sessions.

Multiple regressions related activation for the high-calorie foods vs. cars contrast to percent weight change. Initial BMI was included as a covariate in all analyses. For analyses of 9-mo weight change, weight change during the program was added as an additional covariate.

estimator.value: multiple regression; robust regression using the least median of squares procedure for sensitivity analyses

description.value: High-calorie food images, including sweet and savory foods.
High-calorie sweet foods such as a slice of chocolate cake or cheesecake.
High-calorie savory foods such as a cheeseburger or french fries.
Low-fat foods such as broiled fish or salad.
Pictures of cars used as moderately engaging control stimuli matched to low-calorie food images in ratings of pleasantness.

definition.value: high-calorie food images vs. control images

coordinate_space.value: standard Montreal Neurological Institute (MNI) brain space

interpretations.value: High-calorie food images elicited greater activation than control images in a cluster that included the tail of the caudate nucleus and in cortical regions such as the inferior occipital cortex, inferior frontal gyrus, and superior parietal lobule.

roi_definition.value: All reward ROIs were bilateral and were defined structurally using templates from the WFU Pickatlas toolbox within SPM8 using the AAL or Talairach Daemon atlases; the nucleus accumbens and ventral tegmental area/substantia nigra used predefined spheres and a composite ROI, respectively.

definition.value: high-calorie food images vs. control (car) images

coordinate_space.value: standard Montreal Neurological Institute (MNI) brain space

interpretations.value: In the obese group, reward ROI analysis revealed greater activation to high-calorie food images compared to control images in the insula, amygdala, and anterior cingulate cortex.

definition.value: high-calorie food images vs. control images

coordinate_space.value: standard Montreal Neurological Institute (MNI) brain space

interpretations.value: Whole-brain analysis in the obese group of activation in response to high-calorie food images versus control images revealed many activated regions, including the insula, anterior cingulate cortex, amygdala, inferior parietal lobule, middle occipital cortex, postcentral gyrus, inferior temporal gyrus, and inferior frontal gyrus.

description.value: Result table reporting Session 1 high-calorie food images versus control images for the control group and the obese group in whole-brain and reward-region-of-interest analyses.
